# Automating the Detection of Misleading Design Rationale Generated by Large Language Models

Empirical evaluation of an LLM-based **Verifier Agent** that automatically audits
LLM-generated Design Rationale (DR) for software architecture decisions, extending
the manually-labeled benchmark from Zhou et al., *"Using LLMs in Generating Design
Rationale for Software Architecture Decisions"* (ACM TOSEM, 2025;
[dataset](https://github.com/Eric0052/LLM4DR)).

Paper submitted to **EAI FISAT 2026**.

## What this repo contains

```
src/
  verifier_agent.py       Verifier Agent: prompt construction (zero-shot/CoT/few-shot),
                           Gemini API calls, JSON parsing, per-call logging.
  run_experiment.py       Runs the Verifier over the dataset with resume/dedupe support.
  evaluate.py              Computes Precision/Recall/F1/Cohen's Kappa per IHUM category,
                           macro F1, count-level MAE, and confound analysis
                           (DR length, architecture-decision type).
  make_figures.py          Generates the figures used in the paper.
  list_available_models.py Diagnostic script to check which Gemini models an API key
                           can call (used while debugging free-tier quota issues).

data/raw/                  Zhou et al.'s public LLM4DR dataset (unmodified), see
                           data/raw/DATASET_NOTES.md for schema notes and an important
                           caveat about ground-truth granularity (per-DR argument
                           counts, not per-sentence labels).

data/results/               Full experimental output:
  verifier_predictions.csv    1,200 Verifier Agent predictions vs. ground truth
                               (4 conditions x 300 DRs).
  verifier_raw.jsonl           Full per-argument JSON output for every prediction.
  api_call_log.jsonl           Complete API call log (prompt variant, model,
                               resolved model version, latency, raw response,
                               errors) for every call made during the study --
                               kept in full for reproducibility/auditability.
  metrics_summary.json         All computed metrics (source of truth for every
                               number reported in the paper).
  figures/                     Generated figures (confusion matrix, F1 by category,
                               ablation comparisons).

paper/
  paper_draft.tex             LaTeX source (Springer LNCS format) for the FISAT 2026 submission.
  llncs.cls                   LNCS document class (for convenience; Overleaf usually
                               provides this already).
  figures/                     Copy of the figures embedded in the paper.
```

## Reproducing the experiment

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate   # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env        # fill in GEMINI_API_KEY (https://aistudio.google.com/apikey)
                             # and GEMINI_MODEL (we used gemini-3.1-flash-lite)

python src/verifier_agent.py                                    # smoke test
python src/run_experiment.py --strategies zero-shot,CoT,AI-Agent --variants zero_shot,few_shot
python src/run_experiment.py --strategies zero-shot,CoT,AI-Agent --variants cot --full-ablation
python src/evaluate.py
python src/make_figures.py
```

`run_experiment.py` supports resuming: if interrupted (e.g. by a free-tier quota
limit), re-running the same command skips already-completed predictions and
retries only failed ones.

## Key finding

Supplying the Verifier Agent with the original architecture-problem context (as
opposed to judging the generated DR in isolation) is the single largest driver of
performance: Misleading-detection F1 nearly triples (0.056 -> 0.152) and overall
macro F1 rises from 0.406 to 0.608. Differences between verifier prompting
strategies (zero-shot / chain-of-thought / few-shot) are comparatively small
(macro F1 0.608-0.625). See `paper/paper_draft.tex` for full results and discussion.
